sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Tfnt** ​(*tefnut*) — ‌Moisture, the ‌Dew ​and the ​Rain · ​That ​water, that ​spittle — ‌belongs ​to the ​Egyptian tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued under ​the ‌domain "Moisture, ​Rain, Lions". ​The ​name means ​"That water, ​that ‌spittle"[^1].

**Tfnt** ​— Tefnut ‌— ​is water ‌in its ​gentlest ‌forms: the ​humidity of ‌the ​first morning ​of the ‌world, ‌the dew, ‌the rare ​and ​precious rain. ‌With her ​twin ​Shu, the ‌air, she ​is ​the first ‌pair the ​creator produced ‌— ​and in ​the myth ​that ​names her, ‌the creator ‌spat ​them both ‌into existence.[^2]

​PuniCodex ​records the ‌canonical scholarly ‌spelling ‌**Tfnt** and ‌serves its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/tefnut/). The ​displayed ​form is ‌ASCII-equivalent — ​a ​description computed ​from the ‌displayed ​form itself. ​The plain ​ASCII ‌form *tefnut* ​contains the ‌same ​letters: no ‌recovered diacritics ​or ‌special encoding ‌is claimed. ​The ​work here ​is consistent ​citation, ‌capitalization, provenance, ‌and cultural ​context[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, transliteration, canonical spelling, name variations, and evidence preservation.
sections.body:
The ​name ‌is attested ‌in ​Hieroglyphs ​as **𓏏𓆑𓈖𓏏𓁐**. ​Etymologically ​it ​means ‌"That water, ​that ​spittle"[^1].

‌The canonical ​spelling ‌**Tfnt** ​matches ‌the conventional ​scholarly ​romanization. ​The plain ​ASCII ​form ‌*tefnut* ​contains the ‌same ​letters, ‌so no ​lost ‌diacritics ​or ‌encoding transition ​is ​claimed. ‌The editorial ‌work ‌is ​to ​fix one ‌reviewed ​reference ​spelling, preserve ‌capitalization ​and ​provenance, ‌and keep ​the ‌original ​evidence ​visible. The ​displayed ​form ‌is ASCII-equivalent ‌— ​a ‌description ​computed from ​the ‌displayed ‌form itself.

‌The ‌letter-by-letter ​transformation ‌runs:

- **t** ​→ ​**T** ​— Same
- ‌**e** ​→ ​**—** ​— Vowel ‌not ​written
- ​**f** → ​**f** ‌— ​Same
- ‌**n** → ​**n** ‌— ​Same
- **u** ‌→ ‌**—** ​— ​Vowel not ​written
- ​**t** ‌→ **t** ‌— ​Same

sections.label: Pronunciation
sections.purpose: IPA reconstruction, phoneme breakdown, approximation, kin forms.
sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name ​is **/ˈtɛfnʊt/ ​(conventional)** ​— ‌Conventional ​reading ​— ‌Egyptian ​vocalisation ‌not ​attested.[^1]

‌Phoneme ​by ​phoneme:

- ​**Tf-** — ​Written ​tfn.t; ‌the ​name’s ‌root ​is ‌tf, ​“to ‌spit” ​or ‌“to ​be moist”.
- ​**-n-t** ‌— ‌Conventionally ‌vocalised ​“Tefnut”; ​the ‌feminine ​ending ​marks ‌her ​as ​the ‌moisture-principle.

For ​the ‌modern ​speaker, ​the ​closest ​approximation ‌is: ‌“TEF-noot”

​Kindred ‌and ​historical ​forms ‌of the ‌name:

- ‌**Greek** ‌— ​Τέφνυς ‌(Téphnys)

​Her ​name ​belongs ‌to ​the ​tf-family: ​in one ‌cosmogony ​she ​and ​Shu ‌are ​spat ‌into ​being ‌by ​the ‌creator ‌— ​the moisture ​and ​air ​of ‌the ‌first ​breath.

sections.label: Domains & Attributes
sections.purpose: Sphere of influence, titles, epithets, domain cards.
sections.body:
**Tfnt** ​— Tefnut ‌— ‌is water ​in ​its gentlest ​forms: ​the humidity ​of the ‌first ​morning of ​the ‌world, the ​dew, ‌the rare ​and ‌precious rain. ​With ​her twin ​Shu, ​the air, ​she ‌is the ​first pair ‌the ​creator produced ‌— ​and in ‌the ​myth that ‌names ​her, the ​creator ‌spat them ‌both ‌into existence.[^1]

### ​The ​First Moisture

‌The humidity ​that ​preceded creation’s ‌drying-out; ​twin and ​consort ‌of Shu ​the ‌air.

### The ​Solar ​Eye

As ​the ​Eye of ‌Ra she ‌fled ​to Nubia ‌in ​lioness form ​and ‌had to ‌be ‌fetched back ‌by ​Thoth or ‌Shu.

### ​Lioness of ​the ​Waters

Shown ‌as a ​lioness ​or lioness-headed ​woman ‌— the ​same ​dangerous femininity ​as ‌Sekhmet and ​Bastet.

### ‌Mistress of ​the ‌Dew

Her ​moisture ‌is the ‌world’s lubricant ​— ​the dew ​on ​which the ‌sun’s ‌first dawn ​condensed.

sections.label: Symbols
sections.body:
The ​iconography ‌associated ‌with Tfnt ​concentrates ​in ​a ​small ​set of ‌recurring ​attributes, ​each ‌a ​compressed ‌statement about ​the ‌name:[^1]

- ​**The ​First ​Moisture** — ​The ​humidity ‌that ​preceded ‌creation’s ​drying-out; twin ‌and ​consort ‌of ​Shu ‌the air.
- ​**The ​Solar ‌Eye** ‌— ‌As ​the Eye ​of ‌Ra ​she ​fled ‌to Nubia ​in ​lioness ‌form ​and ‌had ​to be ​fetched ​back ​by ‌Thoth ‌or Shu.
- ​**Lioness ‌of ​the ​Waters** ‌— ‌Shown as ‌a ‌lioness ​or ‌lioness-headed ​woman — ​the ​same ‌dangerous ​femininity ​as ​Sekhmet and ‌Bastet.
- ​**Mistress ​of ​the ‌Dew** — ​Her ‌moisture ​is ‌the ​world’s ‌lubricant — ‌the ​dew ​on ​which ​the sun’s ‌first ‌dawn ​condensed.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
Tefnut’s mythology ​is concentrated at ‌the world’s beginning and ‌in the great ​Eye-of-Ra cycle. As ​one of the ​first two beings ​she needs few adventures ​— but the ‌one she has, ​the flight to ​Nubia and the ‌embassy that retrieves her, ​became one of ‌the most told ​and most illustrated ‌stories of the ​New Kingdom.[^1]

### The Spat-Forth ​Pair (Heliopolitan Cosmogony)

​In the Memphite ​and Heliopolitan accounts ​the creator — ‌Atum or Ra — ​produced his first ‌two children by ​spitting (tf) and ‌sneezing: Tefnut the ​moisture and Shu the ‌air. Their names ​are the verbs ‌of that first ​physiology; the world’s ​atmosphere is the afterbirth ‌of the god’s ‌own body.[^2]

### The ‌Flight to Nubia ​(Eye of Ra ​Cycle)

When the creator ‌grew old, men ​plotted against him ​— and his ‌Eye, sent to ​punish them, abandoned her ​post in fury ‌and fled south ​as a raging ‌lioness. Egypt withered without ​her. Shu or ​Thoth was sent ​to coax her ​home with the ‌*Destruction of Mankind* tale’s ‌rhetoric of flattery; ​her return, pacified, ‌restores the inundation ​and the sun’s ​order.

### The Return of ‌the Goddess (Leiden ‌Papyrus)

The literary ‌composition ‘The Return ‌of the Eye’ ​gives Tefnut’s wanderings their ‌fullest poetic form ​— the goddess ​who leaves, rages, ​is sung back, ‌and returns transformed from ​destroyer to blessing. ​It is the ​mythic template behind ‌every Egyptian pacification ​ritual of dangerous goddesses.

### ​Mother of Nut ​and Geb (Genealogical ‌Theology)

With Shu ​she bore Nut ‌the sky and Geb ​the earth — ‌the second divine ​generation. As grandmother ‌of Osiris, Isis, ‌Seth and Nephthys she ​stands at the ​head of every ​royal pedigree; the ​titulary of kings ‌names her among the ‌oldest company of ​the gods.
